items.head: Caution
items.quote: Vessels are prohibited from anchoring in the sound except in the designated berths.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Trawling is prohibited in these channels and anchoring is only permitted in charted anchorages. Submarine cables also extend from the shore about 0.5 mile NW and NNW, respectively, from Narsaq Kujalleq Church. The alignment of Narsarmijit Entrance Range Beacons (092°), located about 0.5 mile SE of the church, marks the N limit of the anchorage area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Taking a pilot is not compulsory, but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available by making arrangements with the Port Operator. Vessels should send the request for a pilot through Qaqortoq (Julianehab). The pilot boards off Akia or by arrangement.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available by arrangement with the Port Operator. Vessels should send the request for a pilot through Qaqortoq (call sign: OXF) by VHF. The pilot boards off Akia or by arrangement.

notes.quote: The vessel’s ETA is to be advised to the Port Operator 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available by arrangement with the Port Operator. Vessels should send their ETA to the Port Operator 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: There are no pilots, but persons with local knowledge are available. An ETA should be sent at least 24 hours in advance. The port may be contacted (call sign: Ice Central) on VHF channel 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advisable; an unlicensed pilot is available by arrangement with the Duty Officer. Vessels should send an ETA at least 24 hours in ad - vance. The port can be contacted by VHF channel 16.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: That part of Arsuk Fjord approaching Gronnedal is a prohibited area, the seaward limit of which is marked by beacons, in line about 130º, on the N shore of the fjord. No vessel may enter this area without the prior permission of Greenland Command at Gronnedal.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: That part of the fjord, which lies within 2 miles of the port, is considered to be a prohibited area. The seaward limit of this area is marked by beacons. Vessels must receive permission from the Greenland Command Naval Station before entering.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but advisable. A representative, with local knowledge, is available on request. Vessels should send an ETA at least 24 hours in advance. The port can be contacted by VHF channels 13 and 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is recommended. Pilots are normally available from May to October. Vessels should send an ETA at least 24 hours in advance. Vessels must have permission to enter from the Port Operator.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but advisable. The Port Manager is available and will act as an unlicensed pilot on request. The pilot boards off Avatdleq, 1 to 5 miles WSW of At - torssuit Light, and be contacted on VHF channels 13 and 16. Nuuk also provides pilotage for Kangerluarsoruseq (Faeringehavn).

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchoring and any use of gear towed on the bottom is prohibited in the protection zone, which extends 200m on each side of submarine cables and pipelines.

items.head: Pilotage
items.place: Miles NW of Kitdliaraq Light Tower
items.quote: Taking a pilot is not compulsory but is advisable. Unlicensed pilot is available by arrangement with Port Operator. Vessels should send request for pilot through Nuuk (call sign: OX). Pilots meet vessel outside the harbor or at Faltings Skaer, 2.5 miles S of Maniitsoq Light.

notes.quote: Advise the Port Operator of the vessel’s ETA 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Directions
items.place: Miles NW of Kitdliaraq Light Tower
items.quote: Kitdliaraq and the islands NE are reported to be good radar targets. A vessel approaching from S is advised to identify Kitdliaraq and then proceed as already described. At night, approach with Kitdilaraq Light bearing not more than 090°, until in the white sector (004.5° to 011.5°) of Annertusoq Light, which leads safely through the approach to the harbor.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: There are no pilots, but persons with local knowledge are available.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Local residents, with knowledge of local conditions, are available if requested. There is no authorized pilot available, but the harbormaster will assist with berthing.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The military bases are restricted defense areas subject to special regulations. A minimum of 8 hours notice of the vessel’s ETA must be given to the port officials or agents. Vessels should establish contact on RT 2716 kHz at least 1 hour prior to arrival. The harbor is navigable 24 hours from the beginning of July to the end of October.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advised. Unlicensed pilots are available on request and will board in the vicinity of Jacobs Skaer, 2 miles SW of Mollers O Light.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: On nearer approach to the land care must be taken not to be set to the N. On reaching Jakobs Skaer (66°53.9'N 053° 48.6'W) alter course SE of Mollers O until the Praestefjeldet Range Lights, in line bearing 007° and shown from May 1 to August 1, can be brought into line;. The front light, an orange hut, is situated on the S side of Sagdlerssuaq (66°57.0'N., 053°43.0'W.), an island 12m high, lying close offshore; the rear light, also an orange hut, stands on the shore 0.6 mile S of Praestefjeldet.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but advisable. There is no official pilot, but experienced local assistance is available if requested with the ETA message; the pilot usually boards off the harbor entrance.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The harbor is reported to be open from May to December and closed for the winter.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advised. Unlicensed pilots are available on request. The harbor can be contacted by VHF channels 13 and 16. Vessels should send request for pilot with their ETA and arrange the pilot boarding position.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A protection zone, marked by beacons, extends a distance of 200m along each side of the pipeline Anchoring, dredging, fishing, and trawling are prohibited in this area. Disko Island (Qeqertarsuaq)—Southeast Coast

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available on request. Vessels should send an ETA and a request for a pilot at least 24 hours in advance. The pilot can be contacted on VHF channels 9, 13, and 16.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels must inform the Port Operator of their ETA 12 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is recommended. An unlicensed pilot is available on request. Vessels should send an ETA at least 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available upon request.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is optional for coastal vessels entering Davis Straits. Agents are to make arrangements if a pilot is required. Information about navigational conditions can be obtained by radiotelephone from the Quarry Manager, who acts as the Harbor Authority. A 720hp tug/icebreaker is available to assist if required and will break up any thin ice in the vicinity of the berth or entrance to the fjord.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It was once reported that an old whaling vessel had crossed Melville Bugt in the month of June, when the winter ice lay solid along the coast. This crossing was possible only by using an open channel that exists between the pack ice and the shore ice. During favorable times of the navigation season, vessels can navigate along the W coast of Greenland as far N as Etah, close N of Kap Alexander.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory but is advisable. Unlicensed pilots are available by arrangement with the Port Operator. Vessels should send a request for a pilot with the ETA. The pilot boards 1 mile off the harbor entrance.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Vessels making for Upernavik from the S must approach from E of the rocks 14 miles SSW of the harbor and then proceed between Aorrussaq (Hvalo) and Qeqertusussuk (Bruuns O) to the W, and Qaersorssuaq, to the E. Care must be taken to avoid rocks awash and below water, up to 0.25 miles to seaward of Smedeo, an near islet SW of Upernavik Island, before turning into the harbor entrance W and N of Isabel Islets, which lie off the S entrance point.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Naviga - tion is prohibited within this protected area. Exceptions may be made to allow local hunters and scientific expeditions to operate within certain parts of the reserve. The seaward limit consists of a line joining the following positions: 1. Kap Lewis (75°33.9’N., 58°22.5’W.). 2.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: No pilots are available. U.S. Harbor Service personnel provide berthing assistance. Vessels should send their ETA well in advance to both the U.S. Base Authority at Thule and to the Danish Harbor Authority at Dundas.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Navigation is prohibited in the E part of Wolstenholme Fjord. Port of Thule Air Base (Pituffik) (Qaanaaq) (76°32'N., 68°52'W.) World Port Index No. 1000

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Taking a pilot is not compulsory, but is advisable. An unlicensed pilot is available; arrangements are made through the Port Operator. The vessel’s ETA should be sent to port officials 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: For information on Traffic Separation Schemes, Two-Way Routes, and Areas to be Avoided off the SW coast of Iceland, see Iceland—Areas to be Avoided and Iceland—Traffic Separation Schemes in Pub. 180, Sailing Directions (Planning Guide) Arctic Ocean. For information on the TRANSREP Ship Reporting System, see paragraph 9.1.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not available.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 100 gt and is available 24 hours. Vessels should contact the pilot 1 hour prior to arrival by telephone. The pilot boards, as follows: 1. For Keflavik-Njarvik—1 mile off Vatnsnes. 2.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: See Keflavik (paragraph 8.7).

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels must notify the harbormaster’s of- fice of their ETA 96 hours and 24 hours prior to arrival. Ves - sels must contact the pilot on VHF channel 14 or by telephone 2 hours prior to arrival with the details of any dangerous cargo and its quantity. Tugs, with bollard pulls of 4 tons and 14 tons, are available.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: Reported to have no Yokohama fenders, but installed rubber bumpers on pier (2017). Gamla Hofn Tanker Berth Terminal Eyjargardur 72m 13.0m Fuel oil, diesel oil, aviation gas, white spirits, unleaded gasoline, and gasoil. Vessels up to 45,000 dwt, with a maximum draft of 13m, a maximum loa of 200m, and a maximum beam of 32m, can be accommodated.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Caution

items.head: Caution
items.quote: An area centered in position 64°07.0'N, 21°57.2'W, about 0.3 mile SW of T-head fuel pier, is a restricted areas. Sjomannaskolinn Light is no longer in service and has been replaced by Hofdi Light, which stands along the seawall about 05. mile N or Sjomannaskolinn Tower. A large spoil ground area used by port contractors lies SE of Engey Island.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 60m long and all vessels carrying hazardous or dangerous cargo. The pilot boards in position 64°16.0'N, 22°00.0'W. Vessels should advise the pilot of their ETA at least 24 hours in advance. Vessels should contact the pilot at least 3 hours prior to ETA on VHF channel 12.

calls.quote: Vessels should contact the pilot at least 3 hours prior to ETA on VHF channel 12.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: District and harbor pilots are available at Akranes. Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 60m long and all vessels carrying hazardous or dangerous cargo. Vessels should send their ETA to the pilots at least 24 hours in advance. Vessels should also contact the pilots at least 2 hours prior to arrival on VHF channel 12.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available 24 hours.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: A pilot station is located about 1.8 miles SW of Talkni Point, near position 65°37'N., 24°05'W. Pilotage is available. Pilots board in position 65°37.2’N, 24°05.3’W about 2.5 miles NW of the harbor entrance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available. Pilots can board in position (65°43.6'N., 23°38.2'W.), about 2.5 miles W of Langanes.

notes.quote: Pub. 181, Sector 8 135 Vessels must notify their ETA 24 hours in advance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels of any size. The pilot boards 1 mile from the harbor.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available and compulsory. Pilots will meet vessels coming into the port about 400m from the harbor entrance. Messages may be sent through Siglufjordur Radio, (call sign: TFX) on 2182kHZ or VHF channels 24, 26, and 27.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels of over 100m in length. The pilot boards in the following positions: a. 65°43.0’N, 18°06.0’W. b. 65°45.0’N, 18°06.0’W (for Krossanes Pier). Regulations— Use of ship’s bow thrusters is allowed at arrival/departure, in consultation with the pilot. Painting of ship’s hull is allowed from pier/paint raft.

notes.quote: Vessels should send their ETA 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is available upon request. Pilots can be requested via telephone (354- 464-1575). A pilot station is located about 2 miles E of Husavik, near position 66°02.6'N, 17°22.6'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory but is available and recommended.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilots are available for Raufarhofn. Pilotage is not compulsory, however entry to the harbor should not be attempted without local knowledge.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: In clear weather Raufarhafnarhofdhi may be easily identified, and the position of Raufarhofn is further indicated by the termination of the mountains about 3 miles to the S, but in low visibility great caution must be exercised. From N, take care to avoid the reefs surrounding Asmundastadhaeyjar. From a position ESE of the harbor entrance, the initial approach is on the range lights, in line bearing 281°, lead W, passing S of a lighted buoy moored close S of Baka and then close SW of the buoy.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is available 24 hours and recommended. Pilots should be ordered 24 hours in advance and board in position 65°17.5'N, 13°55.0'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all tankers and all vessels 100m long and over. The pilot should be contacted 2 hours prior to arrival by telephone.

items.head: Directions

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is available at any time and is compulsory for foreign vessels, all vessels with dangerous cargo, all cargo vessels, and all fishing vessels over 50m loa and greater than 700 gt. Vessels should request a pilot through Vestmannaeyjar Coast Radio Station at least 1 hour in advance. The pilot boards in the following positions: a. 63°28’00.0’’N, 20°18’00.0’’W. b. 63°26’24.0’’N, 20°11’21.6’’W.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: An area in which anchoring and fishing are prohibited has been established over the entire width of Eyjasund (63º26'N., 20º16'W.) between the mainland of Iceland and the NE coast of Heimaey. Numerous submarine cables and pipelines have been laid in the area. Beacons mark the cable landing places. The charted restricted area encompasses the harbor approach area between Faxasker (63º27.6'N., 20º14.4'W.) and Bjarnarey.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: Anchoring is prohibited within the submarine cable and pipeline area, which begins approximately 7.5 miles SSE of Surtsey and continues SSE for 17. 5 miles. Hellisey, a grass-covered islet, is located 2.75 miles SW of the S extremity of Heimaey. It rises to a height of 130m at the NE end and is fronted by dangerous rocks.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 60m. The pilot station is located in position: 63°51'12.6"N 21°18'06.6"W. Inbound vessels should send pilotage requests 1 hour prior to arrival; outbound vessels send pilotage requests one 1 prior to departure. Vessels should advise ETA 24 hours in advance via e-mail, including the vessel’s Pilot Card.

items.head: Pilotage
